channel.title: Black Agenda Report - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Black Agenda Report (blackagendareport.com)

item.title: The State of Trump’s Union: Geopolitical Economy Hour with Ajamu Baraka | Black Agenda Report
item.description: In this Geopolitical Economy Hour, Radhika converses with one of the foremost left political leaders and Black political activist and journalist in the US, Ajamu Baraka. Together, they understand the current crisis as rooted in the 500-year history of colonialism, racism and racial capitalism.

item.title: Epstein Class vs. Iran: "They’ll Blow Up the World" | Black Agenda Report
item.description: BAR Editor and Columnist Ajamu Baraka joined BettBeat Media, alongside Dr. Gerald Horne, to discuss the US imperialist campaign against Iran amid the ongoing genocide of Palestinians and how the same forces that inflict that violence abroad are reflected in domestic state repression.

item.title: Venezuela's Bolivarian Revolution and Struggle for Independence in Puerto Rico | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Brianna Alvarado Ramos of Diaspora Pa’lante Collective discusses the challenges of the revolutionary struggle in Venezuela and the fight for Puerto Rico's independence from U.S. colonialism.

item.title: Gerald Horne on The Hawaii Coup and the Roots of US Imperialism in the Asia-Pacific Basin | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Dr. Gerald Horne joins us from Houston to discuss his latest work, The Counter Revolution of 1893: The Hawaii Coup and the Roots of U.S. Imperialism in the Asia-Pacific Basin. He connects 19th-century U.S. imperialism with the present-day aggression against Iran.

item.title: Black Agenda Radio March 6, 2026 | Black Agenda Report
item.description: In this week’s segment, we discuss past and present U.S. imperialism, analyzing struggles to protect Venezuela’s Bolivarian Revolution and to bring independence to Puerto Rico. But we begin with a conversation about a new book exploring the 1893 coup, which seized the kingdom of Hawaii and ultimately made it a U.S. state, with Dr. Gerald Horne, who also connects that history with present U.S. actions in Iran.

item.title: The Black Alliance for Peace Condemns the U.S. War on Iran | Black Agenda Report
item.description: The United States attack on the Islamic Republic of Iran began on February 28. Our guest provides analysis on this U.S. aggression from an anti-imperialist and Black left perspective. Erica Caines is a writer and organizer in Baltimore and the DMV and is the Field Operations and Membership coordinator of The Black Alliance for Peace, and founder of #LiberationThroughReading, providing African children with books that represent them. She joins us from Baltimore.

item.title: Navid Zarrinnal’s Perspectives From Iran | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Navid Zarrinnal is an Iranian journalist and host of The Colony Archive podcast. He joins us from Tehran to discuss the US and Israeli aggression and explains why the left must be in solidarity with Iran.

item.title: Black Agenda Radio March 13, 2026 | Black Agenda Report
item.description: This week’s segment is devoted to the United States latest war of aggression against the Islamic Republic of Iran. We hear the perspectives of a U.S. based activist and organizer with Black Alliance for Peace about that organization’s anti-imperialist perspective and their opposition to this current attack and all U.S. attacks on sovereign nations. item.title: Iran, UAE, Sudan, and Crises in the Horn of Africa | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Abayomi Azikiwe, Editor of Pan-African Newswire, discusses events in the Horn of Africa. The U.S. war against Iran is impacting the United Arab Emirates (UAE), whose Rapid Support Force proxies are carrying out atrocities in Sudan. Also, colonial borders are disputed, Ethiopia faces a renewed conflict in the Tigray region, and Israel's recognition of the breakaway region of Somaliland violates African sovereignty.

item.title: Iran Resists the U.S./Israeli Attack | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Bahman Azad, president of the US Peace Council, joins us to discuss the US/Israeli war of aggression against Iran. The US has committed war crimes by assassinating Iranian leaders, and bombing schools, homes, and other civilian targets. But Iran is a military power that can strike Israel and US assets in the region.

item.title: Black Agenda Radio March 20, 2026 | Black Agenda Report
item.description: In this week’s segment, we discuss the U.S. and Israeli war against Iran and crises in the Horn of Africa. Sudan is experiencing a humanitarian catastrophe created by United Arab Emirates proxy forces seeking to unseat that country’s government, while colonial borders and decades-long conflicts between nations in the region remain unresolved. But we begin with a conversation about Iran's resistance to US/Israeli war of aggression.

item.title: Combating the Lies and Propaganda that Fuel the USA-Israel War on Iran | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Jacqueline Luqman, Margaret Kimberley, Netfa Freeman, and Gus Griffin were among the panelists joining Your World News Media to discuss the lies and war propaganda that fuel the brutal war of aggression against Iran.

item.title: Community Control DC, A People’s Platform for Collective Self-Determination | Black Agenda Report
item.description: Pan African Community Action (PACA) recently released a plan for political empowerment in Washington DC, "Community Control DC, A People’s Platform for Collective Self-Determination." Oliver Robinson of PACA provides analysis.

item.title: Cuba Solidarity and Resistance to the U.S. Embargo | Black Agenda Report
item.description: We're joined by Suzanne Adely of the National Lawyers Guild and the International Association of Democratic Lawyers and Corinna Mullin of the US Peace Council and Anti-Imperialist Scholars Collective as they discuss Cuba's resistance to the 67-year long embargo and the importance of solidarity with that nation.

item.title: Black Agenda Radio March 27, 2026 | Black Agenda Report
item.description: In this week’s segment, we hear about an effort to build community-based power and self-determination for a Black working-class Washington, DC community. But we begin with a report on conditions in Cuba from two activists who recently participated in the flotilla solidarity movement. They discuss how the accelerated US embargo is impacting the Cuban people, who nonetheless remain committed to resistance and maintaining their nation’s sovereignty.
